identity_marker: colorful Stride Rite sneaker with standard white laces and a visible logo
continuity_anchors: brightly lit indoor playroom with a soft wooden floor and warm natural sunlight
video_goal: Demonstrate how to guide a child in tying their Stride Rite sneakers using the visual 'bunny ears' two-loop method.
single_prompt: In a brightly lit indoor playroom with a soft wooden floor and warm natural sunlight, an adult places a colorful Stride Rite sneaker with standard white laces and a visible logo on a child's foot, pulling the laces straight out. The adult gently guides the child's hands to grip one lace in each fist. From the child's perspective, they cross the left lace over the right to form an 'X', then tuck the top lace under and pull outward to tighten the base knot. The child pinches the left lace to form a 'bunny ear' loop, then does the same with the right lace. Holding both loops upright side-by-side, the child crosses the right loop over the left to form a new 'X'. An adult finger taps the small triangular gap at the bottom of the crossed loops, prompting the child to push the top loop through the gap. The child grasps both loops and pulls them outward simultaneously to tighten the knot. Finally, from a high angle, the child proudly pats the finished double-loop knot resting securely on the sneaker.
